about: Remarks on the pressure of dots, milestones in reach, the field, the pitch and the light.

bunnings: {b}: {dots} dots faced in a row. A patient examination.
{dots} WITHOUT A RUN FOR {b}. HE'LL BE COUNTING.
{b} HAS GONE {dots} WITHOUT SCORING. THE BOWLER IS ON TOP.

bunnings.text: {dots} DOTS IN A ROW. IN THIS FORMAT THAT'S A SMALL CRISIS.

lorry: {dots} dots now for {b}! Nothing loose to work with!
{dots} DOTS! {b} NEEDS TO GET OFF STRIKE!
{b} CAN'T GET IT AWAY! {dots} IN A ROW!

lorry.text: {dots} DOTS IN A T20! THE CROWD'S GETTING RESTLESS!

grog: {dots} scoreless deliveries faced by {b}. The bowler is closing the options.
{dots} DOTS. HE HAS TO FIND A SINGLE, ANY SINGLE.
THE BOWLER HAS FOUND {b}'S OFF STUMP. {dots} DOTS.

bunnings: {b} has faced {dots} dots in succession. Every run must be earned.
{dots} DOTS NOW. THE SCOREBOARD HAS FORGOTTEN {b}.
{b} IS STUCK. {dots} BALLS WITHOUT A RUN.

bunnings.text: {dots} DOTS. A T20 BATTER CAN'T AFFORD MANY OF THOSE.

lorry: {dots} dots to {b}! The pressure is building with every ball!
{dots} DOTS! THIS IS AGONY FOR {b}!
STILL NOTHING! {dots} BALLS! SOMEBODY HELP HIM!

lorry.text: {dots} DOTS IN A ROW IN A TEST! WHAT A DUEL!

grog: {b}: {dots} consecutive dots faced. He needs a single to break the hold.
{dots} DOTS. HE'S LOOKING FOR A BAD BALL AND THERE ISN'T ONE.
{b} NEEDS TO ROTATE THE STRIKE. A PUSH AND RUN, ANYTHING.

grog.text: {dots} DOTS. IN THIS FORMAT, THAT'S WORSE THAN A WICKET.

bunnings: {b} has faced {dots} dots now. The bowler is making him work for every inch.
{dots} DOTS. HE MAY HAVE TAKEN ROOT.
{b} HAS NOW FACED {dots} WITHOUT A RUN. REMARKABLE, IN ITS WAY.
lorry: {dots} scoreless balls faced by {b}! Something has to give!
{dots} DOTS! I'VE NEVER SEEN ANYTHING LIKE IT!
{b} IS TRAPPED! {dots} BALLS! THE BOWLER'S GOT HIM IN A CAGE!
grog: {dots} dots faced by {b}. The bowler is narrowing his scoring options.
{dots} DOTS. EITHER HE BREAKS THE SHACKLES OR THE SHACKLES BREAK HIM.
THIS IS THE MOMENT A BATTER GETS OUT. {dots} DOTS DOES THAT TO YOU.

bunnings: {b} on {runs}. A hundred is close; the next ball still needs playing.
{b} ON {runs}. THE NINETIES CAN BE A NERVOUS PLACE.
{need} SHORT OF A HUNDRED. {b} MUST BE THINKING ABOUT IT.
lorry: {b} is on {runs}! Just {need} short of three figures!
{b} IS IN THE NINETIES! {need} TO GO! I CAN'T WATCH!
SO CLOSE NOW! {b} ON {runs}!
grog: {b}, {runs}. Keep the scoring options open; don't let the hundred dictate the shot.
{runs}. THE BOWLERS WILL TRY TO KEEP HIM ON STRIKE AND MAKE HIM WAIT.
{b} NEEDS {need}. PLAY THE SAME WAY THAT GOT YOU HERE.

bunnings: {b} on {runs}. A fifty within reach, with patience.
{b} ON {runs}. THE FIFTY BECKONS.
{need} MORE FOR {b}'S FIFTY.
lorry: {runs} for {b}! {need} away from the half-century!
{b}'S ON {runs}! THE FIFTY'S RIGHT THERE!
COME ON, {b}! {need} FOR THE FIFTY!
grog: {b} on {runs}. No need to force the milestone.
{runs} FOR {b}. DON'T CHASE IT. IT WILL COME.
{b} NEEDS {need}. THE BOWLERS WILL TRY TO MAKE HIM WAIT.

bunnings: Four wickets for {w}. One more would complete a fine spell.
FOUR FOR {w}. ONE MORE FOR THE HONOURS BOARD.
{w} HAS FOUR. HE'LL WANT ANOTHER.
lorry: {w} has four! One more for a five-wicket haul!
{w} IS HUNTING NUMBER FIVE! COME ON!
ONE MORE FOR {w}! THE FIVE-FOR IS ON!
grog: {w} hunting a fifth. The captain will want to keep the pressure on.
{w} ON FOUR. KEEP HIM ON. HE'S IN RHYTHM.
FOUR FOR {w}. THE TAIL IS IN; HIS FIFTH SHOULD COME.

bunnings: {field}
lorry: Look at the field! {field}
grog: {field}

bunnings: That kept low. Something else for the batter to consider.
KEEPING LOW NOW. THE PITCH IS TIRING.
UNDER THE BAT. IT WAS NOT BOUNCING TODAY.
THE BOUNCE HAS GONE OUT OF THE PITCH.
lorry: That stayed down! Watch the bounce on this surface!
IT'S SHOOTING ALONG THE GROUND!
THAT KEPT SO LOW! LIKE A RAT UP A DRAINPIPE!
THE PITCH IS DYING! IT'S KEEPING LOW!
grog: Low bounce on a wearing surface. The straight ball remains a threat.
LOW BOUNCE: BOWL STUMP TO STUMP AND THE BATTER HAS TO PLAY EVERYTHING.
THE CROSS-BAT SHOTS ARE OFF THE MENU ON A PITCH THIS LOW.
THE BOWLED AND THE LBW ARE IN PLAY. ATTACK THE STUMPS.

bunnings: A little extra lift there. Worth noting.
THAT ONE TOOK OFF. A LIVELY SURFACE.
STEEPLING BOUNCE. HE DIDN'T EXPECT THAT.
THE PITCH HAS SOME LIFE IN IT YET.
lorry: That climbed! There's still life in this pitch!
THAT REARED UP! LOOK AT THE BOUNCE!
IT'S FLYING THROUGH! THE KEEPER'S TAKING IT ABOVE HIS HEAD!
WHAT BOUNCE! THE QUICKS WILL LOVE THIS!
grog: Extra bounce on that delivery. The batter must allow for it.
EXTRA BOUNCE. BRING IN A SHORT LEG AND A GULLY.
WITH THIS BOUNCE, BACK OF A LENGTH IS THE WICKET BALL.
THE BATTER HAS TO PLAY WITH SOFT HANDS ON A PITCH THIS LIVELY.

bunnings: We've seen one keep low and another climb. Not entirely predictable.
ONE KEPT LOW. THE NEXT MAY NOT.
THE PITCH IS BEHAVING RATHER UNPREDICTABLY.
THE CRACKS ARE HAVING THEIR SAY.
lorry: Low, then high! This surface is asking awkward questions!
THAT ONE SHOT THROUGH! THIS PITCH IS A MINEFIELD!
LOOK AT THE BOUNCE! UP AND DOWN LIKE A YO-YO!
THE BATTERS DON'T KNOW WHAT'S COMING!
grog: Low bounce and extra lift in this innings. The cracks complicate the length.
UNEVEN BOUNCE MEANS BOWL STRAIGHT. THE PITCH WILL DO THE REST.
ON A PITCH LIKE THIS, PLAY LATE AND UNDER YOUR EYES.
THE BOWLERS SHOULD JUST HIT THE CRACKS AND WAIT.

bunnings: The cracks are opening as this pitch wears. Patience will matter.
THE CRACKS ARE WIDENING. THE SPINNER HAS NOTICED.
YOU COULD LOSE A COIN IN SOME OF THOSE CRACKS.
THE PITCH IS BREAKING UP. AS PITCHES DO.
lorry: Look at that worn surface! Every ball could bring a chance!
LOOK AT THOSE CRACKS! THE SPINNER'S RUBBING HIS HANDS!
IT'S SPINNING OUT OF THE CRACKS! WATCH OUT!
THE PITCH IS FALLING APART!
grog: Those widening cracks give the spinner another problem to pose.
AIM AT THE CRACKS AND LET THE PITCH DO THE WORK.
THE CRACKS GIVE THE SPINNER TWO DELIVERIES: ONE THAT TURNS, ONE THAT DOESN'T.
BATTING LAST ON THIS WILL BE A NIGHTMARE.

bunnings: Afternoon light, lengthening shadows. A fine setting for the contest.
THE AFTERNOON SUN IS SETTLING IN.
A WARM AFTERNOON. THE FIELDERS ARE LOOKING FOR SHADE.
lorry: Lovely afternoon light! Now, who makes the most of it?
WHAT A LOVELY AFTERNOON FOR CRICKET!
THE SUN'S OUT AND SO ARE THE ICE CREAMS!
grog: Long afternoon shadows across the ground. Keep watching the length.
THE AFTERNOON IS USUALLY THE BEST TIME TO BAT. THE PITCH IS AT ITS BEST.
TIRED LEGS IN THE AFTERNOON. THE BOWLERS WILL FEEL IT NOW.

bunnings: The evening shadows stretch across the ground. A lovely light.
THE SHADOWS ARE LONG NOW. A LOVELY LIGHT.
EVENING. THE CROWD IS THINNING.
lorry: Evening light now! Still plenty of cricket in this contest!
LOOK AT THOSE SHADOWS! WHAT A SIGHT!
THE LIGHT'S GOING! PICK IT UP IF YOU CAN!
grog: Long shadows in this evening light. Concentration still matters.
IN THIS LIGHT THE BALL IS HARDER TO PICK UP. BOWL STRAIGHT.
EVENING. THE NEW BALL WOULD BE DANGEROUS NOW.
